I play this game on Steam Deck. It runs well at 60 FPS—flawless. Nothing to complain about; it’s a great experience. However, there are several things you should be aware of before buying this game.

[b] Difference from Rev 2 [/b]: It’s nearly the same. The main gameplay difference is balance, and there are more characters (17 vs. 25). The other difference is in the story (covers the first half of the overall story)—it’s mostly cutscenes with no gameplay mixed in. It feels like playing a visual novel.

[b] Online mode [/b]: Dead. If you decide to buy this, make sure you have friends or a community to play with. This game doesn't have [b] Rollback [b]

[h3] So I recommend buying GUILTY GEAR Xrd REV 2 for a more complete experience. [/h3]

[b] About unlocking characters [/b]: It’s no coincidence that the publisher sells DLC to unlock them. Farming currency in this game is a real pain. Unlocking three characters costs about 600k, while a hard arcade run gives around 8k per match. If you only play casually for a few matches per day, progress is very slow. I recommend following a guide to farm more efficiently (M.O.M mode, challenges, and finishing the story can give you around 100k)

Siapa YB?
Bagi yang buta, dia adalah penglihatan. Bagi yang lapar, dia adalah daging. Bagi yang haus, dia adalah air. Karena YB adalah teladan kebajikan manusia yang tiada tandingannya, baik di masa lalu maupun masa kini, dia paling bercahaya dalam cinta, pujian, dan sanjungan. Dalam keadaan terjaga maupun tertidur, aku tak boleh lupa bahwa YB adalah anugerah besar, dan untuk membalas kebaikannya siang dan malam, aku hanya perlu memikirkan bagaimana menunaikan kesetiaanku.
Keringatnya adalah parfumnya hidupku. Senyumnya adalah pil serotonin bagiku. Gerak-geriknya adalah penenang jiwaku. Tangannya adalah kekuatanku. Wajahnya adalah galeri keindahan. Dadanya adalah awan-awangku. Kakinya adalah karya seniku. Pusarannya adalah kebanggaan dan kebahagiaanku. Secara keseluruhan, dialah raison d’être-ku — alasan keberadaanku.
Jika Arap berpikir, aku setuju. Jika YB berbicara, aku mendengarkan. Jika Arap memiliki sejuta penggemar, aku salah satunya. Jika YB memiliki sepuluh penggemar, aku salah satunya. Jika Arap hanya memiliki satu penggemar, itu adalah aku. Jika YB tidak memiliki penggemar, maka aku tidak lagi ada. Jika seluruh dunia menentang Arap, maka aku akan menentang seluruh dunia.
Aku akan mencintai YB hingga napas terakhirku, di masa lalu, masa kini, masa depan, dan di semua kemungkinan semesta.

GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN- stands out immediately with its striking visual style. The game uses 3D models rendered to look like high-end 2D animation, creating a distinct aesthetic that still holds up. Every character motion feels handcrafted, and the presentation gives fights a sense of weight and spectacle rarely matched in the genre.

The combat system delivers the depth the series is known for. Its mechanics—Roman Cancels, Burst, Faultless Defense, and character-specific systems—offer a high skill ceiling while maintaining clarity. Inputs feel sharp, movement is responsive, and the game’s pace balances aggression with tactical decision-making.

Character variety is one of the title’s strongest points. Each fighter brings a unique toolkit and playstyle, from rushdown to zoning to highly unorthodox mechanics. This diversity encourages experimentation and makes matchups feel fresh. The roster may be smaller than later entries, but every character is distinct and carefully designed.

The story mode takes a cinematic approach, offering a fully animated narrative rather than traditional fights with cutscenes. While gameplay is minimal, the production quality is high, and it serves as a strong introduction to the world and characters for newcomers. Fans of the series will appreciate the lore focus and voice work.

Training tools are robust and accessible. The tutorial breaks down fundamental concepts clearly, and the mission mode helps players learn advanced mechanics step-by-step. This makes the game more approachable than older Guilty Gear titles without sacrificing depth for seasoned players.

Online play was solid for its time, though modern rollback standards make the delay-based netcode feel dated. Matches can still be enjoyable with good connections, but it is not as consistent as later Arc System Works releases. Despite this, the online community remains active enough for casual play and learning.

Overall, GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN- remains a standout entry in the fighting-game landscape. Its exceptional art direction, deep combat system, and bold character design make it worth playing even years later. It serves as both a strong introduction to the Xrd series and a compelling experience in its own right.

Guilty Gear Xrd -SIGN-, developed and published by Arc System Works, is a landmark entry in one of the most technically demanding and stylish fighting game franchises ever made. It marks a significant evolution in the series, introducing a breathtaking new visual direction while refining the high-speed, mechanically intricate gameplay that has defined Guilty Gear for decades. Rather than abandoning its complex roots, Xrd -SIGN- reimagines them for a new era, blending accessibility and depth in a way that few fighters have achieved. From the moment the rock-infused soundtrack kicks in and the cel-shaded 3D characters explode onto the screen, the game declares itself as both a visual revolution and a reaffirmation of Arc System Works’ mastery of the genre.

The first thing that captures attention is the presentation. Arc System Works made the bold decision to shift from hand-drawn 2D sprites to fully 3D models rendered with stunning cel-shading techniques that perfectly mimic traditional animation. The result is a visual experience that feels like a living anime—one that never breaks immersion even when the camera swoops and spins during special attacks or finishing moves. Each hit bursts with energy, each character animation carries deliberate exaggeration, and the transitions between gameplay and cinematic moments are seamless. It’s not just technically impressive; it’s artful, with every frame showcasing the studio’s dedication to style and motion. The rock soundtrack, a long-standing Guilty Gear hallmark, complements this perfectly—each track pounding with guitar riffs that match the adrenaline of the battles and reflect the rebellious tone of the series.

Mechanically, Guilty Gear Xrd -SIGN- finds a perfect balance between being accessible to newcomers and deeply rewarding for veterans. The fighting system retains the depth and complexity that longtime fans expect, including mechanics like Roman Cancels, Bursts, Faultless Defense, and the Tension Gauge, but it refines their execution and makes them more approachable. Movement feels fluid, attacks connect with satisfying weight, and every mechanic serves a tactical purpose. The pacing of combat is fierce and deliberate, allowing aggressive rushdown styles and methodical spacing play to coexist. Each character feels wholly unique, from the technical mastery of Zato-1’s puppet-like mechanics to the brutal straightforwardness of Sol Badguy’s close-range pressure. The roster may not be as large as later Guilty Gear entries, but the depth of individuality among the fighters more than compensates for its size. The game encourages experimentation, and mastery comes from learning not only your chosen fighter but also how to read and respond to the rhythm of your opponent.

Arc System Works also put great effort into making the game welcoming without sacrificing the intricacies that define Guilty Gear. The extensive tutorial mode and mission challenges offer clear, detailed explanations of every system, providing practical scenarios that help new players grasp core mechanics while allowing veterans to refine advanced techniques. Few fighting games at the time offered such a robust onboarding experience, and it became one of Xrd’s most praised features. The inclusion of local multiplayer and online play ensures that the game’s competitive potential is fully realized, though early versions of its online lobbies and matchmaking systems were somewhat clunky compared to modern standards. Still, the netcode held up well enough for most players to enjoy stable, intense matches that showcased the brilliance of its combat engine.

Beyond the battles, Guilty Gear Xrd -SIGN- attempts to expand its world through an ambitious story mode. Rather than following the traditional arcade narrative structure, the game presents its story as a fully animated cinematic experience, complete with voice acting and visual novel-style presentation. It’s an interesting experiment—one that allows the lore and personalities of Guilty Gear’s eccentric cast to shine—but its lack of interactivity may disappoint players expecting gameplay within the story. Nonetheless, the production values are high, and it serves as a deep dive into the series’ complex narrative universe, tying together old threads while introducing new characters who would become mainstays in later entries.

From a competitive standpoint, Xrd -SIGN- was a significant turning point for the fighting game community. It revitalized interest in the series after years of absence and laid the groundwork for the later, more expansive Guilty Gear Xrd -REVELATOR- and Rev 2 updates. The precise hit detection, balanced character design, and refined mechanics made it an ideal platform for tournaments, with many players praising its responsiveness and the sheer satisfaction of its combos and counterplay. While the game’s smaller roster and early content limitations may have restricted its longevity in comparison to its successors, its influence cannot be overstated—it redefined what a modern 2D fighter could look and feel like, setting a standard that inspired other franchises to follow suit.

Ultimately, Guilty Gear Xrd -SIGN- is more than just an entry in a long-running series; it’s a statement of artistic and mechanical excellence. It reimagines the essence of Guilty Gear without diluting it, maintaining the chaotic beauty, technical mastery, and rebellious energy that have always defined the franchise. Every punch, slash, and explosive Overdrive move feels deliberate, rewarding, and cinematic, while the visuals and sound combine to create an atmosphere of raw intensity and stylish bravado. It’s a game for both the dedicated fighting game enthusiast and anyone who appreciates the craftsmanship of interactive animation. Years after its release, Guilty Gear Xrd -SIGN- remains a testament to Arc System Works’ ability to innovate within tradition, proving that even in a genre saturated with contenders, passion and artistry can still set a game apart as something truly exceptional.

GUILTY GEAR Xrd -SIGN- é um dos títulos que melhor representa o que é um jogo de luta técnico e visualmente impressionante. A direção de arte em cel-shading é um espetáculo à parte, com animações fluidas e detalhadas que fazem cada luta parecer uma cena de anime.

Quando o assunto é platina, o jogo deixa bem claro que ela não é para qualquer um. As exigências incluem não só completar o modo história e os modos arcade com vários personagens, mas também encarar os temidos desafios de combo. O modo Challenge vai testar execução e precisão ao extremo, principalmente com personagens que exigem inputs avançados.

Além disso, há os troféus multiplayer, que exigem um bom desempenho online. Para quem não está acostumado com jogos de luta competitivos, essa etapa da platina pode se tornar um verdadeiro obstáculo.

É o tipo de 100% que só vem com treino constante, repetição e domínio técnico. No final, é uma platina que te faz sair do jogo melhor do que entrou. Quem conquista ela pode dizer com orgulho que entende de fighting games.
